utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to all. May I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Prosecution Thomas Hannis and Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence. Our expert will be joining us after the first break. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours for Zupljanin Defence Igor Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could the usher escort the witness to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Nielsen. I remind you that you're still on your oath. Mr. Zecevic, you may continue your cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you will recall yesterday we talked about the situation in the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP in the time period covered by the indictment and before the division of the MUP. In paragraphs 49 to 52, you refer to a document. This is a document of the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP. It's probably a state security service document, and it is 65 ter document 31 from December 1991. Do you remember that you referred to this document in these paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, isn't it a fact that the document, this alleged report by the state security service about the security situation in December 1991 does not refer anywhere to the existence of the Patriotic League or the Green Berets as an armed wing of the Party for Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't reviewed the document recently. I note that it's a document of several pages, so I cannot a priori agree with that. That may well be the case. I would, however, not call the document -- or not describe the document as an alleged report by the state security service. It is a report by the state security service, and I can see by the ERN number on the report that it's a report that I personally recovered in the offices of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska in 2002, and I therefore have no doubt to -- no reason to doubt the authenticity of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't have any reason to doubt the authenticity of the document, and it's possibly a matter of the interpretation. I tried to suggest to you that I am doubting the objectivity of that document and the content but not its authenticity. I don't really want to show you the document now. I don't want to waste time, and I am just referring to it for the sake of the reference. That's why I gave you the number. But tell me, are you aware that the Patriotic League and the Green Berets existed already in 1991 as the armed forces of the Party for Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of documents from 1991 that refer to groups called the Patriotic League and the Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, are you aware that as early as June 1991, the SDA formed a council for national defence of the SDA? Did you ever see such a document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that fact. I am not an expert on the internal structure or workings of the Party for Democratic Action. Excuse me, Party of Democratic Action is the correct term.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. If you're not an expert for the internal workings and structure of the Party of Democratic Action, then I would like to draw your attention to your footnote 33 in your report in relation to paragraph 20 of your report. And there you say in footnote 33 that there were rumours that Muslims were being trained in Croatia and that they were taking part in actions against Serbs in Croatia, and then you say that those -- it was proved that the rumours were false, untrue, and it was established that the Muslim police officers were present in Croatia as part of routine training, but nonetheless, the rumours served a propagandistic, were a tool in the propaganda strategy of the SDS. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, Mr. Nielsen, that the assertion that the Party of Democratic Action was sending policemen of Muslim ethnicity for training to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible, and I do not exclude that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, this is the Ministry of the Interior. You are an expert, as you say, for the Ministry of the Interior, and it would not be unusual for you if one of the parties in the state was sending some members of its forces for training to another state?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to some degree it occurs to me that there is a question of what constitutes another state as you put it at this time, but, yes, I'm certainly aware that there were allegations that the Muslims or Bosnian Muslim officials in the SRBiH MUP were sending personnel of Bosnian Muslim ethnicity to Croatia for training. That's why I mentioned that in footnote 33. And I'm also aware that there were simultaneous allegations that Croatian -- ethnic Croatian personnel were going to Croatia to receive training, and I'm also aware that there were allegations simultaneously that Bosnian Serb personnel in SRBiH MUP were receiving training in Serbia at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you very clearly, I think, but you are giving me an answer that does not correspond to my question. I asked you about the party, not about the leadership in the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP of Muslim ethnicity. Please look at the document 1D01-0410. This is in your binder that we prepared for you. This is tab 6 in your binder, actually. 1D01-0410. That is not the document, 1D01-0410. I apologise. It's an error. Just one minute, Your Honours. Not to waste any time, let us now look at 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please be asked to repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Would you be good enough to repeat the number, because the interpreters didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. 1D00-4681, but I think that it is also P424.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab number 7, Mr. Nielsen. Mr. Nielsen, this is an SDA Sarajevo document, Marsala Tita 7-a/IV is the address. Now that we're on this topic, are you aware that that was the SDA address? You went through so many documents. Was this the address of the SDA in Sarajevo in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible. I don't know what their address was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, the document is dated 8th of July, 1991. The democratic -- Party of Democratic Action, the signature of the secretary, the stamp, and it is titled "List of Candidates for Training as Special Forces in the Republic of Croatia MUP," and then there is a stamp also at the bottom with the date. On the next page and the following pages, up to page 14, it's in the e-court, we have a total of 463 members of the special forces who went for training to the MUP in the Republic of Croatia. If you look through the document, they -- the names of the people are of people who come throughout the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Fojnica, Sarajevo, Vlasenica, Gorazde, Nevesinje. The age of the people on the list is of people who are fit for duty, able-bodied men. And then on the last page, which he is page 14, it says: "Inclusive with number 463, you will then get a continuation of this list in seven days." Do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I have, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you told us that you went to Bosnia and Herzegovina on several occasions to obtain documents which in your opinion were important in order to be able to write your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were aware of the fact that there was an allegation and a serious concern among the Serbs and the leadership of the MUP among the Serbian population in 1991 that the Party of Democratic Action was secretly sending some young men from the reserve police forces for training to the Croatian MUP. You did know about that, didn't you, and that's why it's there in your report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you concluded in your report that those rumours proved to be untrue, and this is what is stated in your footnote 33. Now when I show you this document, do you still stand by your assertion that these rumours proved to be false?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would point out that the statement that I make in paragraph 33 relates to the particular document written by Vojislav Pecanac on the 25th of July, but certainly viewing the document that you are showing me now, I don't have any problem concluding, seeing this document for the first time, that there was certainly -- there were several a number of ethnic Muslims from Bosnia and Herzegovina undergoing training on the territory of the Republic of Croatia for -- that is Special Police training, as you state.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nielsen. I am interested, if you -- to know if you would agree with me that then this was not done by the Ministry of the Interior at all but that this was done by the Party of Democratic Action, which was making its own party army; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that we're conflating a couple of points here. As I told you, I'm not an expert on the SDA or its doings during the period from 1990 to 1992, and when I pointed that out, you informed me that I should have been aware of such things based on my knowledge as a MUP expert. You're now telling me that this, in fact, has nothing to do with the Ministry of Internal Affairs about but, rather, has to do with the Party of Democratic Action. As I've stated earlier, I think it's very important that we all realise that for the period from the multi-party elections, and we agreed on this yesterday, from 1990, November 1990, until 1992, the lines between parties, all three parties, the SDS, the SDA, the HDZ, and the officials --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Mr. Nielsen, I have to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- [overlapping speakers] increasingly vague.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would kindly ask you to focus on my question and to give me short answers. I'm going to do my best to put my questions in such a way that you can reply with a yes or no. I asked you about your assertion in your report in footnote 33 that there was -- there were rumours that in 1991 that the Party of Democratic Action was sending members of the MUP for training to Bosnia and Herzegovina, to training to the MUP in Croatia secretly. You assert in your report that these rumours proved to be false, unfounded, and you are telling me that you did not see this document. That means that you did not even want to check these rumours, but you just wrote in your report that the rumours were false. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is your assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's argumentative and that misstates his earlier question. His earlier question was, "I'm interested if you -- to know if you would agree with me that then this was not done by the Ministry of the Interior at all but that this was done by the Party of Democratic Action which was making its own party army. Isn't that right?" Well, it's a compound question for one thing. Was it done by the Ministry of the Interior or the Party of Democratic Action and also was the Party of Democratic Action making its own party army? Those are -- those are at least two separate questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, it would perhaps be helpful to the witness and to the Chamber if you were to, as it were, step back and eliminate the argument from your question and put the questions in a way that the witness could intelligently answer, could helpfully answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I will show you document 1D00-4826. This is document number 9 in your binder. You see, Mr. Nielsen, this is from the same period, the 11th of July, 1991. It's an entire book of documents, if I can put it that way, of the SDA. It says here "Instructions for candidate," and then the name of the candidate. There is a number, et cetera. It is addressed to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia, and it says in the text: "In keeping with the joint agreement of authorised representatives of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the MUP of the Republic of Croatia and instructions for employment of entry-level candidates at the education centre of the Republic of Croatia MUP, the Party of Democratic Action - Sarajevo, recommends the above candidate to attend a course at your centre. "Yours faithfully. "Handwritten for Hasan Cengic, SDA Secretary." And then there's the signature and stamp. There are more than 100 basically identical documents here. Now I'm putting a question to you, a very brief and simple question. Do you stand by what you said in footnote 33 that these rumours about the SDA sending candidates for training to the MUP of Croatia were false and that that was used for propagandist purposes by the Serb Democratic Party? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already revised that conclusion earlier in the answer to your previous about the document, but I would point that I don't mention the SDA in particular in that footnote.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is precisely why we had this previous exchange of views, and then Mr. Hannis objected, because you keep on trying to avoid the SDA, and I am showing you documents that bear the letterhead of the SDA, and the documents say that the SDA recommends the above-mentioned candidate, et cetera. That is -- how should I put this? That is our only point of contention at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I certainly agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir. Thank you, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If -- if I may, Mr. Zecevic. Dr. Nielsen, for my own perhaps very simple mind, and no doubt this is something which Mr. Hannis can return to in re-examination, your last-but-one answer when Mr. Zecevic asked you for a yes or no and your answer was, I already revised that answer in the question to your previous document, but I note that I don't mention the SDA in particular in that footnote. The -- may I ask, as Mr. Zecevic did, for a yes or no answer to his question? As I said, the explanations could come later. Perhaps, as I said, it's my own inability to understand complex matters. Do you need to -- would you need to repeat -- me to read the question back to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you. I'm perhaps a bit loquacious, and yes, I agree with Mr. Zecevic, and the short answer to his question was yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you know that Mr. Alija Delimustafic, minister of the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina, mobilised the reserve police force in June 1991. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I state in paragraph 21 of my report, and there was a discussion ongoing between Mr. Delimustafic and Mr. Zupljanin as -- in July 1991 in which Mr. Zupljanin was urgently requesting mobilisation and at that point Delimustafic refused to approve Mr. Zupljanin's repeated requests to mobilise, if we're talking about July 1991. Oh, June you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I read your report. It is a fact that Mr. Zupljanin, because of the situation that was in the border area that was the Republic of Croatia, I mean, that entire area had serious security problems, and therefore, what was required was replenishment, more personnel. However, I'm asking you about the general decision on the mobilisation of the reserve police force in the entire territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991 by Minister Alija Delimustafic. Perhaps that was later in September 1991. You are referring to a document of Mr. Radovan Karadzic. If I remember correctly in your report, you refer to that.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My memory calls me to recollect that the Delimustafic ordered mobilisation took place as you are suggesting probably sometime around September after this discussion, because he was resisting mobilisation during the summer of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll show you the document, 1D01-0915.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we leave the document which is currently on the screen something just caught my attention in the entry that is shown on the monitor, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- it says: "In keeping with the joint agreement of authorised representatives of the MUP," which I understand to be the Croatian MUP on the one hand and the BiH MUP on the other, the Party of Democratic Action hereby recommends a certain person to attend a course. I wonder if we could elicit from the witness the nature of that joint agreement to which the document refers. I mean, was there a joint agreement between the Croatians and the BiH at the time that would allow political parties to submit candidates for training? That sounds peculiar to me, but maybe if we can ask the witness about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you for your suggestion. Of course I'm going to put that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you heard the question of His Honour Judge Harhoff. In your report I did not find any references to the existence of some agreement between the representatives of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the MUP of the Republic of Croatia. Do you know about the existence of that kind of an agreement?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that such agreement -- that such an agreement existed, but it is correct that Mr. Hasan Cengic does seem to be referring to such an agreement having existed or being in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, if there was an agreement between the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia, in your view, since you are an expert for Ministries of the Interior, wouldn't the only logical and normal thing --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection. He's been proposed as an expert on the Ministry of the Interior for the RS MUP, not for the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hannis, I assume that Mr. Nielsen has special knowledge that refers to internal affairs, what Ministries of the Interior do in a general sense and that that makes it possible for him to be an expert for the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. I wanted to put a very general question which is fully logical. That is something that he should be aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I only note the Defence has been challenging from the beginning Mr. Nielsen as an expert on the RS ministry, but now he wants to qualify him as an expert on the Republic of Croatia. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It strikes me, Mr. Hannis, that the -- your -- your objection is, with respect, technically correct having regard to the basis on which this witness is proposed, but I see no difficulty with Mr. Zecevic's question if what he is in fact asking the witness is based on his admitted area of expertise, whether by analogy or -- or by comparison. He could -- yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, if there's an agreement between two Ministries of the Interior, in your view do the ministries then communicate between themselves or through state organs, or do they do that through some political parties and party secretaries?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge based on the 1990 Law on Internal Affairs that was valid in Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time and not being familiar with the relevant law that was in force at the time in Croatia, that law in Bosnia and Herzegovina foresaw the ability for ministries to communicate through state organs, ministry to ministry. However, again after November 1990, the line between party activity and MUP activity is extremely blurry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I am putting it to you that there is no logic, and it's not based on the law either, if there's a -- an agreement between ministries that some political party should send candidates for training to another ministry.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's entirely possible, and I'm predisposed to agree with you that that was the de jure situation. I'm indicating based on my expert knowledge of the situation that unfortunately the de facto situation was quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know, but, Mr. Nielsen, yet again we go back to your report and the conclusion you accepted and revised a few moments ago. If that was the de facto situation, then how come you didn't know about it when you wrote your report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I made it very clear that I revised my conclusion based on the document that you showed me today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But we've agreed on that. Now I'm asking you about the time when you wrote the report. As you said a moment ago, if that was the de facto situation, then I'm interested in the following: How come you, as a person who read so many documents and who did such a lot of research, in view of the facts that are referred to in your report, how come you did not come across the basic information that that was what the situation was, in fact?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I had come across the document that you proffered this morning at an earlier stage, I probably would not have -- or definitely would not have put that conclusion in that footnote.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to tell you what I am putting to you. You did not find it because this entire operation of sending people for training to Bosnia-Herzegovina [as interpreted] by the SDA was kept secret?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to object to the question. I think that mischaracterises what the document itself says. The SDA is proposing candidates. Now, that's being sent to the Republic of Croatia, to the ministry of Croatia. He hasn't established yet, from what I've heard, that the SDA sent the candidates. These are candidates nominated by the SDA pursuant to an agreement that's referred to in this document between the MUP of Croatia and the MUP of SRBiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And I do apologise to my colleague Mr. Zecevic and to the Chamber. I think the -- it was a misspelling of Mr. Zecevic, I think. It's page 15, line 22. Instead of Bosnia-Herzegovina it should say Croatia, training to Croatia instead of Bosnia-Herzegovina by SDA. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honours, I realise it's a procedural matter. I know Judge Harhoff left a short while ago. I don't know. In my past experience, I think you may need to make a finding pursuant to Rule 15 that it's in the interests of justice for the remaining two Judges to continue to sit without Judge Harhoff. I just bring that to your attention for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't want it to be a matter of appeal later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Hannis. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thank Mr. Hannis for that intervention, and the -- I note for the record that the Chamber is continuing to sit under the provisions of Rule 15 bis in the absence of Judge Harhoff. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I know it's been a couple of minutes, but could I hear your response to Mr. Hannis's objection to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just bear with me, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, I shall withdraw this question. I accept Mr. Hannis's objection. In this way, I tried to cut the time of the cross-examination, as it were, but obviously I will have to show this witness all the documents involved so that we would have a clear situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And it is noted for the record that the Chamber is again fully constituted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, I would like to suggest that 1D01-0915, the document I showed to the witness, be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Document 010915 shall be marked as Exhibit 1D121 marked for identification. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1D01-1147.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, that is your document in tab 6. Sir, you see this document? It is dated the 11th of July, 1991. This is what it says: "To the Executive Board of the SDA, to the president." And it says: "Instruction for sending candidates to the training centre of the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia." And then in the text says that they are enclosing a copy of the instruction on the method of hiring candidates for police officers, beginners in the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia with your obligation to introduce the candidates to it. And also, they say here that every candidate has to bring along a referral from the party. That's the document we saw a few moments ago, 1D00-4826. That's the one that you looked at a few moments ago. That is the referral provided by the party. And then there is a reference here to the address of the training centre of the MUP of the Republic of Croatia and also the deadline, the time by which the candidates are supposed to show up at that locality. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I would point out that the document you provided to me in tab 6 does not correspond to the document which you are discussing that I do see on the screen, but, yes, I do see the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. It must be some kind of a mistake, but do you see it on the screen? Do you see what I've read out to you? You do see it, right, from the document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So, this -- this is the instruction that is provided by the -- to the Executive Board of the SDA, and it explains what the instructions are -- or, rather, what documents are needed, what documents are needed by each and every candidate, and the key document is a referral from the party; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, please. Could it be admitted into evidence if there are no objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D01-1147 is admitted as Exhibit 1D122. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you the referral again. It is 1D00-4826. You saw it a few moments ago, and I omitted to tender it. So we have this document now on our monitors, and it pertains to the document I mentioned just now, that is, 1D00-4826, the one that is going to appear on our screens right now. That's your tab 9, I believe. You see that this document is called "Referral for candidate," and it is in accordance with the document that we looked at a moment ago, and every candidate has to bring such a document along when going to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to suggest -- or, rather, I would like to tender 1D00-4826.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 1D00-4826 shall be given Exhibit 1D123. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After that, I showed you document 1D00-4681. That's a list of candidates, and I would like to ask that that document be admitted into evidence as well. That is a list of candidates for specialised training. Remember that I showed you that document when I asked you about the address of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And you mentioned yourself, Mr. Zecevic, that this was P424, already admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I do beg your pardon, Your Honour. I'm sorry. We have a bit of a problem with our list of documents indeed. That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to show you document 1D00-4697. Rather, 1D00-4739. I'm sorry. That is your document in tab 10 according to my list. Ministry of the Interior, the 31st of July, 1991. It says: "Personnel Department of the MUP. "Subject: List of attendees of the 6th course for policemen in training who abandon the course or left the course." And then we have a list of 62 persons, obviously of Muslim ethnicity. Do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: From this document we can see that some of the attendees left this course and the MUP of the Republic of Croatia was now informing that some of them had given back their equipment and provides the exact date when they left or signed out. The signature is by the head of the school -- actually, it's signed for the chief inspector, Josip Strmotic.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see. That is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document if there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document number 1D00-4739 shall be given Exhibit 1D124. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to show you 1D00-4704. This is in your tab 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we also see the English version, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a large document. It's dated the 8th of August, and the heading states: "MUP of the Republic of Croatia. List of attendees of the 6th course for rookie policemen." And then there is an alphabetic list of the attendees by the battalions. The total number is 285. Perhaps there could be more. And it seems that for the most part the attendees are of Muslim ethnicity. We can see that from the document. For example, from page -- actually, the last ten pages of the document lists mostly persons of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm waiting for your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was saying -- I was saying the last ten pages are mostly Muslims, aren't they, on the list, Muslim by ethnicity for the most part?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be the case. I would note that most of the last pages are actually lists of people who left the course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Who did not leave the course you mean. It says: "The list of attendees of the 6th course for rookie policemen who did not leave the course on the 16th of August, 1991."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. That was, sorry, my mistake, and I would point out that the entire document, I would agree with you, is predominantly Muslims, and the rest are no Croats and there is no Serbs on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I -- I do have -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, is it your understanding or -- that all these people, the 285 people, are coming from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not manage to do that analysis to compare that with the lists that we have from the SDA, but I absolutely do intend to conduct this analysis and to prepare that for our defence case and also for our closing statement. It is our position that most of those who were Muslims came from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and not from Croatia. I do not rule out the possibility that there are some Croats who also came from Bosnia and Herzegovina, but the ethnic Croats by some sort of logic would not get there via the Party of Democratic Action, which is a Muslim party, but they would be getting there by means of the Croatian Democratic Union community. So in any case, we are going to make this analysis and compare the names of these persons so that we would then be able to provide you with a more detailed overview of who was actually sent by the SDA for training to the MUP of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So it's correct to say that you can't tell just from this document who comes from where. This document does not give that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document only states their ethnicity. It does not say where they are actually from. It only states their ethnicity. But if we analyse that together with the other tendered documents, then we can establish where they came from and if they were sent there by the SDA or upon instructions of the SDA, and this is why I he would like to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would initially request that this only be marked for identification at this point. I don't think there's been an adequate nexus to show that it's probative to some point in issue. And if I may, I go back. This all relates to footnote 33 in Mr. Nielsen's report on page 14 of the English where he made reference to: "In June 1991, rumours circulated that Muslims were training in Croatia and also participating in combat actions against Serbs in Croatia. These rumours were proven always was it was clarified that Muslim police officers were present in Croatia as part of routine training." Now, Mr. Nielsen has made a concession that he was partly mistaken about that in light of the document he was shown, but I didn't raise this when 1D122 was admitted, but 1D22 is the document that's dated 11 July 1991. It's the instruction for sending candidates to the training centre of the Ministry of Interior of Croatia, and the first paragraph says: "Herewith enclosed we are sending you a copy of the instruction on the method for hiring of candidates for police officers, beginners in the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia." Now, if that's a correct translation, then this seems to be talking about some Muslim officers who are going to Croatia to be trained as beginners in the Ministry of Interior for Croatia. If that's the case, I don't see how that's relevant to the argument about Muslims from Bosnia training in Croatia and then trying to become part of the police force in Bosnia, if that's the argument being made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: What I thought was happening, and Counsel will correct me if I've got it wrong, is that the -- having regard to and bearing in mind the status of the witness as an expert, is that Mr. Zecevic was laying -- seeking to lay the foundation for such of his case as would challenge the conclusions at which the expert had arrived, and I share Mr. Hannis's reservation about adding paper, because of course at the end of the day it's the Chamber which is going to have to wade through this. But I thought that Mr. Zecevic should be permitted of set of this foundation. Is that what you're about, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I then put the direct question? Is it for the purpose of testing the credibility and the expertise of the witness, or is it for the purpose of showing that the Bosnian Muslims were siding up with the Croats and tendering their common police officers for training in Croatia so that they could be ready for combat against the Serbs? I mean, where are you going with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the aims was to test the credibility of the witness. The witness changed his conclusion in his report already, so that part is over. Now, we tried to establish the situation which led to the partition of the MUP in March 1992, and we say that by -- by this involvement of the SDA into sending their members to MUP of Republic Croatia -- Republic of Croatia to undergo the police training, they were creating their own police force and their own army behind the back of the Serbs in the Ministry of -- of Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And we -- I believe we have already established that the Serbian -- that the Serbian officials in the ministry of Bosnia-Herzegovina and other Serbian party leaders were protesting on a number of occasions because of -- of these wrong-doings as they saw it in the -- at the time, and that is basically what Mr. Nielsen confirms in his -- his report. I don't know if I have satisfied Your Honours with the -- with my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, partly and partly not, because I think you're reading something into the testimony of this witness that I have not picked up, namely that this was a clandestine operation that was going on behind the back of the Serbs. You may recall a while ago I raised the issue of this agreement that apparently had been concluded between the Croatian MUP and the Bosnian MUP, which surprisingly would allow the political parties to send candidates rather than the competent police authorities in both countries or both parts of what was then Yugoslavia. So that is one thing that -- that to me contradicts your assertion that the witness has testified that this was all going on behind the backs of the Serbs. And secondly, I think the witness, but you may take it up with him again, I think the witness at one point said that also the Serbian political party was sending Serb police officers from Bosnia to training in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe it would be more appropriate if the witness was excused while we are making these explanations, at least from the point of view of Defence, but be it as may be, it -- Your Honours, the problem we see here is that allegedly there is an agreement between the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Ministry of Interior of Republic of Croatia, whereby the witness who went to 200 or so thousand pages could not find this agreement. So therefore whether this was an oral agreement or any other kind of agreement, there is no record of that. The witness confirms that there were allegations, and in his report he says these allegations were false. Now, we have established that these allegation were is obviously not false, and I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Not all of them. About Muslims engaging in combat in Croatia against the Serbs? That's one of -- part of the footnote.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will come to that also. What we are saying is that the witness, based on these document, confirmed that had he had these documents in his view he would confirm that the SDA was sending candidates for the training in MUP of Republic of Croatia. Now, what -- what we are saying is that it is obviously something very wrong with the situation where there is -- there is allegedly an agreement which nobody has saw or which doesn't exist in any -- in any documents between two ministries, and then none of the ministries is communicating with each other, but the Party of Democratic Action is sending candidates to the Ministry of Interior of Republic of Croatia, and that is how we -- we claim with a certainty that this was done in secrecy and behind the back of the Serbian members of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, in the interests of time, and we're about -- it's time for the break, let's not lose sight of the issue as to whether this document should be exhibited. Do I understand the -- from what you said earlier, that you and -- we'll have to hear what Mr. Hannis has to say on the other side, that this something that really needs to -- that we really need to devote time to when we return and, as you say, possibly in the absence of the witness, or is it a much -- assuming, of course, that Mr. Hannis stands by his objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, what we can do is as the time for the break is now, we can -- probably Mr. Hannis and I can discuss this issue and then report to you before the witness is brought to court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If we need to exchange some arguments, then the witness can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- called. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may report the result of our communication, Mr. Hannis and mine. There are three more documents which are the lists of the -- of the participants of this training in Croatia, and these are 1D00-4745, 1D01-0893, and 1D01-0929, and we have agreed, because these documents are really just the lists of the -- of the names and with the indication to which battalion they were attending the course, that all these three documents be MFI'd, and we will then deal with it in the course of this trial later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just ask the parties, is it a contested fact, and I'm looking to the Prosecution, do you contest or disagree about the fact that the SDA was sending Muslim police candidates for training in Croatia? Is that something that we need to argue about?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't disagree with that, but these particular documents, I don't know if we can tie these documents to that fact. This may refer to some other group of Muslims that are training in the Republic of Croatia. I haven't been able to satisfy myself looking at these documents that they refer to the group that we have some evidence of being named as candidates by the SDA to attend some training in the Republic of Croatia with the Croatian MUP, but I don't know that these are those guys. That's why I've continued to have an objection up to this point, and it seemed to me the best resolution was to have them MFI'd for now, subsequently to be linked up perhaps later in our case or in the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we'll mark them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, 1D00-4745 shall be marked as Exhibit 1D125 marked for identification. 1D01-0893 shall be marked as Exhibit 1D126 marked for identification. And finally, 1D01-0929 shall be marked as Exhibit 1D127 marked for identification. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May the witness be brought back?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, just a few more questions on this topic. Mr. Nielsen, isn't it true that the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina had its school for training? It was called the secondary school of the Ministry of the Interior, and it was at Vraca in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it was customary that members of the police and course attendees from the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina went there for training; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to show you document 1D01-0932. It is your tab 15, and you will refer to it in your footnote 33. That is a document of the CSB Banja Luka, Official Note, signed by Mr. Pecanac, Vojislav Pecanac. It's dated the 25th of July, 1991, and it says here in paragraph 2 that on the 25th of July, 1991, a certain Suad Music, born on -- born in 1962, came to the Banja Luka CSB premises of his own initiative, and he informed them that a certain Kunic Isak, known as Iso, a member of the SDA is organising the taking of Muslims to training in the Croatian MUP that was taking place in Zagreb, and he's saying that he found out that the training was two months and that a salary was paid out to attendees there, that it was financed by Arab Emirates, and if they have any problems they should report to a certain Omer Basic in a mosque in Zagreb. You saw this document when you wrote your report, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and I cite it, as you note, in footnote 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Inter alia, it says in paragraph 4 that this same Music who came to provide information to the CSB claims that in the heading of the questionnaire that has to be filled out when they go to the Zagreb MUP it says SDA and that it is signed by Hasan Cengic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That, of course, corresponds to the documents that you saw a few moments ago like the referral from -- for candidates. They're all signed by Hasan Cengic and it all says SDA in the heading; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to the referrals for cadet training for police in Croatia. That's s correct, it does correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections I would like to have this document admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D01-0932 shall be marked as Exhibit 1D128. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And let me show you one more document, 1D01-0935. That is document number 16 in your binder. It is tab 16 in your set of documents. This is a document of the CSB Bratunac of the 16th of March, 1992. It is Senad Hodzic, the chief of the public security station, who is writing this, that is to say that he is an ethnic Muslim. He is writing to the chief of the CSB Tuzla in March. The number is 362/92. And then he is talking about the order to step up the reserve police force, and then in paragraph 3 it says: "After we started conducting the required checks, we came to learn that there is a certain number of military conscripts of Muslim ethnicity who had stayed in Croatia within the training of the Croatian MUP. We do not know on whose order or recommendation, but it is believed that Serb citizens do not have enough trust in such future members of the reserve police force. We would therefore like to know," et cetera, et cetera. He's actually asking for information for instructions as to what to do with such military conscripts, and he says: "In relation to this problem, we telephoned CSB Tuzla and the MUP, and we have nevertheless decided to request in writing your opinion with respect to taking on such military conscripts for war assignment." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that you are reading accurately from the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sir, you will agree with me that this document evidently shows that the chief of the public security station from Bratunac, an ethnic Muslim, his name is Senad Hodzic, in March 1992 he does not know that what was organised was some kind of course for military conscripts of Muslim ethnicity in the MUP of the Republic of Croatia. Isn't that obvious from this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you state, he's an ethnic Muslim, and, yes, he is claiming that he did not have any knowledge about this matter. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He even says specifically, "We do not know on whose orders or recommendation." That is what it says in this document; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that is what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I don't mind admitting the documents and I see the relevance to the point that you are trying to make, but it also seems to me that the witness doesn't know the document, and the only thing he can do is to confirm that you have read out correctly from it. Should we MFI it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked the witness for a conclusion regarding the document. It was you, Your Honour, who asked me to explain why it is that we claim that this was an operation that was being carried out by the Party of Democratic Action, that was being done behind the backs of Serb personnel in the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina and in full secrecy, at that. From this document we see that even the chiefs of public security stations of Muslim ethnicity did not know about it. So I read the document to the witness because I assumed that he hadn't seen it before because he did not mention it in his report, and the witness did agree with me that this document proves that the chief of the public security station, Senad Hodzic, in March 1992, is unaware of the existence of this kind of course for members of the police who are of Muslim ethnicity, and I absolutely believe that this corroborates, like the previous document, our position that this was not done on the basis of co-operation with the ministry but, rather, it was done secretly in co-operation with the SDA. That is why I'm referring to this, and that is why I think it's relevant, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I didn't say it was not relevant. On the contrary, I think I expressed my agreement with you that it is clearly something that goes to proof of the point that you are trying to make. The only hesitation I had is whether we could admit this document through this witness, because apparently he doesn't know anything about it. He has never seen it before, and the only thing that he could confirm was that you were reading out correctly from the document, which is why I then said that we perhaps should MFI it. I'm not against admitting it and it's clearly relevant to your point, but there is a system which we're trying to apply that directs us to admission [overlapping speakers] witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely agree with you, Your Honour, but this is an expert witness is bringing -- a witness who the Prosecution is bringing in as an expert. So from that point of view, since he is an expert in police matters or the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, and of course in part of his report he speaks of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the division of that MUP. Then I thought that since it was the OTP that disclosed this document to us, I thought that this was a good opportunity to introduce the document through this witness, although he hadn't seen it before. He now has an opportunity to comment on it. The document has identical status to all the other documents that the witness refers to in his report. I thought that Mr. Hannis was on his feet in order to object if I managed to understand what he was doing. However, I did not hear what the objection was, if any. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I was going to object to its admission. I agree with you. I think the appropriate treatment of this document at this time is to MFI it. All Mr. Nielsen said was, "You've read it correctly. That is what it says." Mr. Zecevic in his argument said, "From this document we see that even the chiefs of public security stations ..." We see one chief. We don't know when this guy became chief. He said that he obtained information that a certain number of Muslim military conscripts who have spent time in Croatia on part of a training within the MUP of Croatia. Well, apparently the information was available somewhere so to make the argument that this shows that it was done in secrecy can't depend alone on this document. For that and other reasons, I think at this time the best course would be to MFI this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 1D01-0935 shall be given Exhibit 1D129 marked for identification. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, we discussed something a while ago, and I moved on to the question of mobilising the reserve force in September 1991, and then because of the questions put by the Trial Chamber, we returned to the question of sending SDA candidates to these courses. I shall remind you of what this was. It was your footnotes, number 50 and 51, in your report, that is. Since we've -- since we've already introduced document 01-010915, an instruction provided by Mr. Alija Delimustafic, I'm interested in 1D01-0921.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have it in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is your tab 20 and your footnote 50. 1D01-0921. That's the document. Do you see this document dated the 26th of September, 1991? The document was signed by assistant minister of the interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Momcilo Mandic, and he submitted it to the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the government, the MUP, and so on. Do you see the document? You commented upon it in footnote 50.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that Mr. Momcilo Mandic is providing his view and comment on the decision of the Presidency about allowing the Ministry of the Interior, on minister's orders, to engage additional police reservists from the contingent of undeployed military conscripts? And he says on page 2 in the Serbian text, he says that the conclusion of the Presidency is such that in fact it makes it impossible to increase the reserve police force without any limits imposed. Do you remember this document? Do you remember the comment?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that that is in contravention of regulations, because the Presidency can, by its own order, increase the number of reserve policemen only in accordance with the decision taken by the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And since the last government decision that is there dates back to 1987, and that's on the last page, therefore, Mr. Mandic proposes that in keeping with this government decision of 1987, this decision -- or, rather, this conclusion of the Presidency be adjusted to the letter of the law and government decisions; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that document Mr. Mandic also says that there are cases when the police is being manned by volunteers without any preliminary checks. Do you remember that from that document too?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that there is the possibility and well-founded fear that such personnel would be impossible to control; right? That is also on page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 1D01-0921 shall be given Exhibit 1D130. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In footnote 51 you commented document 1D09 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the number please be repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab number 18, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. 1D01-0913.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a letter written by President Karadzic in which he instructs Municipal Boards of the political party to instruct persons of Serb ethnicity to respond to the call-up for the reserve police force. Do you remember having commented upon this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do comment upon that document in paragraph 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic expresses his anxiety here that if Serbs do not respond to the mobilisation and call-up that there could be a Muslim police and that that would be some kind of a basis for a civil war; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please tender this document as well into evidence, please. [In English] Pardon. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Admitted and marked for what it's worth.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 01-0913 shall be marked as Exhibit 1D131. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, if we analyse the situation where we have the Muslim ethnic cadres being sent for training to the MUP of the Republic of Croatia and we have the call-up of the police reserves, as Mr. Mandic says, to an unclassified, unrestricted level, in your opinion, the concern that the police or its reserved force would be turned to some sort of armed force, to a military force, is really well grounded. Is it well grounded?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Karadzic cites some very relevant circumstances for why there should be concern about mobilisation. In that context I would point out that it's interesting and relevant that he is, and the SDS by extension, are now opposing the same kind of mobilisation that they themselves were calling for, albeit on a different numerical basis, in the summer of 1991, and I would also point out that as I stated earlier today and yesterday this is an all-around deplorable situation in which Muslims are being trained in Croatia, as you have shown me and which I agree with you and in which as I, in fact, cite in footnote 33 in the subsequent documents, Serbs are being trained with the knowledge of Mr. Karadzic in Sremska Kamenica, in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I thought that we had agreed that the request by Serbs for the mobilisation of the reserve forces referred to specific parts of north-western Bosnia and Herzegovina due to security problems facing them because of the war in Croatia. Isn't this correct, and did you not agree with that point?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly agree with you, and that's what I meant, but perhaps unclearly, when I said that they meant to do so on a different numerical basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, can you please tell me if you know that the Muslim side, other than this, was also acquiring weapons from the depots of the MUP and from the HDZ? Did you see documents indicating this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be specific if -- by what you mean by the "Muslim side"? Are you referring to the Muslims in the SRBiH MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am thinking of the Party of Democratic Action as a party and its members.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would certainly not surprise me given that Croats, Muslims, and Serbs at this point in their respective political parties were receiving weapons from sympathetic members of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen documents where the Ministry of the Interior is issuing any of the national parties weapons from its depots, weapons or equipment for their use?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have certainly seen such documents from 1991 and retrospective documents from 1992 and 1993 which refer to the issuing by the Ministry of Internal Affairs to members of the Serbian Democratic Party, and it would not at all surprise me if the same were the case for the Croat Democratic Union and the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, can you please tell me, Mr. Nielsen, when you mentioned the members of the Serb peoples who allegedly went for training to Sremska Kamenica, did you have any particular document in mind when you said that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what that was?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I based that observation on several documents. The easiest one to refer to since we've been dealing for quite some time with was footnote 33, are the -- I believe it's the second conversation between Radovan Karadzic and unknown male in which he's informed by the unknown male that Serbian cadres are being trained in Sremska Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I wasn't clear enough. When I say document, I am thinking of a written document. I'm not thinking of any intercepts. I'm not thinking of articles from the newspaper, television reports, or anything like that. Did you ever see a document like the ones that I showed you about the Party of Democratic Action which would confirm what you are claiming?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen other documents outside of the categories that you have mentioned that show that members of the SDS-supported Serbian defence forces, called the SOS, in the Banja Luka area underwent training in Pancevo and also in Sremska Kamenica. Both in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But these are not MUP members, if I understood it correctly, but members of the SDS. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are persons who were paramilitary members and who later constituted a large portion of the CSB Banja Luka Special Police Unit. So in that sense I find it to be analogous to the allegations which I believe to be accurate that some Muslim or Croat paramilitaries later became Muslim or Croat police officers with SDS or HDZ report -- support.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, can you please tell me, Mr. Bruno Kvesic -- Mr. Branko Kvesic and Mr. Bruno Stojic were members of the then leadership of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that from September 1991 they were members of the Crisis Staff of the HDZ, the Bosnia and Herzegovina Crisis Staff of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that fact, but it would not surprise me at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a document. This is document 1D110. You will see from the document that Jerko Doko was the defence minister of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that he also was a member of that Crisis Staff. Do you have the document in your set of documents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I found it at tab 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Twenty-three. Very well. Can you please look -- I mean, you've seen that Mr. Stojic, Kvesic, Jerko Doko are here. Do you recognise anybody else here from the Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP? This is in the first paragraph, just underneath the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that Branko Kvesic and Bruno Stojic were both very high-ranking members supported by the HDZ and who were full time employees of the MUP at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will see on page 2 that the position of the Croatian Democratic Union from September 1991, in paragraph 2, is that it is just a question of time when war will break out in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they are calling attention to the seriousness of the situation, and they're asking the Crisis Staff to direct their attention to the defence of the Croatian people. You haven't looked at this document before, have you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not. I'm quite certain it's been dealt with by my colleague who dealt with the establishment of Bosnian Croat MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To flesh out the situation even further before we come to the key question of the division of the MUP, you are aware that a certain number of Serbian policemen from the Sarajevo centre were first mistreated and then they were finally forced to resign and place themselves at the disposal of the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of that incident and similarly ethnically motivated incidents at police stations throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina during that period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is your footnote 95 and document 1D00-2736. This is the document to which you referred in your footnote 95, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the last page of the document, this is page 5 in the e-court, in the last paragraph it states that -- it's just above the signature. I apologise. The last section of the text where there are the signatures then of these employees of Serbian ethnicity. In the last paragraph it is stated that they are being placed at the disposal of the Sarajevo SUP until the definite resolution of their status. As of that day, they are no longer performing their duties in the Stari Grad Security Centre. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have would like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 1D132. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, isn't it true, and I think that you also refer to this in a couple of places in your report, that it was specifically the Serbian personnel in the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP who insisted on professionalism and legality in the operation of the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that Serb personnel also, in addition to certain members of Muslim and Croat ethnicity, issued calls for professionalism and respect of legality during this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true, and I think that you even mention that somewhere in your report, that Mr. Karadzic criticised the members of the Ministry of the Interior of Serb ethnicity precisely because they were overly insisting on the respect for legality and professionalism?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and as I state in paragraph 15, he also said that even if 90 per cent of the employees of SRBiH MUP were of Serb ethnicity, it wouldn't make much of a difference. And he says that they followed the law and the regulations of MUP too much for their own good.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that at the Assembly session of the 24th of March when Mr. Stanisic was appointed minister - this was in 1992 - he also advocated professionalism in the work of the MUP? This is also referred to in your report. This is P198, page 7, paragraph 1 of the Serbian text and page 8, last paragraph of the English text, but I do not wish to spend time, so I don't think it there's any need to show that to the Trial Chamber. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, but, sir, it occurs to me that in my response to the previous question, I made an answer that is based solely -- on a conclusion in my report that is supported solely by intercepts, so perhaps I have to withdraw that conclusion if I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I absolutely agree that you can withdraw that conclusion if it does refer to an intercept. I'm not going to base anything on that myself either. I did ask you, though, to answer this question. This question does not refer to the intercept but refers to the minutes of the Assembly session of the 24th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I remember that, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, in view of the fact that you are an historian by training, I am surprised that these historical events which are of key interest to us in this case - I'm thinking about the division of the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP - you did not place them in the historical context and the events that were going on in that period.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that case my response would be to remind the Court that the -- this report was prepared for the Krajisnik case, and it was my understanding for the Krajisnik case, and indeed also until very recently for this case, that the Court and all parties would have the ability to get that context to which you refer from the report of Patrick Treanor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the context. We know what the context is, and as to whether Mr. Treanor will come or not, that is up to the Prosecution, but I'm asking you, when you were working on your report, why did you not place the events that you deal with in your report in a historical context?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I think he's answered the question about why he didn't put that in his report. It was because he understood that that was going to be addressed by Mr. Treanor and Mr. Treanor's related report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, from what I know, the report by Mr. Treanor refers to the historical context and some other facts. Since the Prosecution will not be bringing Mr. Treanor to testify and will not be exhibiting his expert report, they obviously consider that context to be beyond dispute and that the -- that it is well known to the Chamber. So I'm interested in why does Nielsen not place in a historical context the events he deals with in his report. It's not a matter of whether he knows or does not know the historical context, but it's a question of the influence of the events that we're familiar with on his conclusions in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
