utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen has answered the question about why he didn't include it in his report, and Mr. Nielsen has no control over about what decisions the Prosecution made about whether or not Mr. Treanor will be called because of the limitations on the Prosecution's number of hours, number of witnesses, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, the day before you talked with Mr. Hannis about the Cutileiro Plan, you do not mention the Cutileiro Plan in your report. I assume that the reason for it is the same one that you have just given us for other contextual facts to which I was pointing.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, although you may be familiar with the fact that I was cross-examined about the Cutileiro Plan in Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. If you were examined about the Cutileiro Plan in the Krajisnik case, why then in the revision or addition that you did for the Stanisic/Zupljanin case, i.e., this case, did you not include the facts relating to the Cutileiro Plan in this report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For precisely the reason that I gave previously, namely my understanding that other witnesses, in particular Mr. Treanor and perhaps also Dr. Donia, would deal with that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your expert knowledge, then, you are placing in the context of some kind of collective effort in order to affirm the Prosecutor's theory of the case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. The collective effort is indeed present. That's the T in team, leadership research team, and that means that we collectively seek to break up very complex issues into analytically manageable chunks so that we have one person who is doing the Bosnian Serb leadership, one person doing the Crisis Staffs. I'm the one who does the MUP, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Don't you think that in this way when you split it up into segments you are losing a key connection with the actual real events on the ground and the reasons why some things actually happened?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree, because I make it part of my job -- I should say, I made it a part of my job to read, on a regular basis, the analytical products produced by my colleague experts and in that way try to the keep, to the best of my ability, the actual real events on the ground, as you refer to them, in my mind as I performed my own analysis of MUP documentation. The alternative would be to have one absolutely massive report dealing with everything from A to Z, and I don't think that's feasible for any one person to undertake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, isn't it true, and I think you said that the day before yesterday, that you looked at the Cutileiro Plan and the documents, last week when you came to prepare for this testimony? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: How is it possible that in your report you deal with the division of the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP without mentioning at any point in your report the Cutileiro Plan, which from September 1991 was based on the tripartite principle and the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina into three entities?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we have a clarification about what Mr. Zecevic is referring to when he says the Cutileiro Plan? Is there a particular document that he can hand to the witness and show him as being the Cutileiro Plan that he's referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do intend to show it to the witness. I am just trying to lay the basis for further questions and all the documents that I'm planning to show him in relation to the Cutileiro Plan. The only assertion here is that the Cutileiro Plan existed from September 1991, and that is information that can be found on Wikipedia on the internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If there's a document from September 1991 that is called the Cutileiro Plan, I would like it to be shown to the witness so he can understand and answer the question in context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Zecevic, the witness should first be asked about his familiarity with this. I'm not sure that the -- any purpose is served as to why -- I keep coming back to the fact that he is proffered as an expert witness, that why the report which is before us -- we're dealing with what is in the report, not what is not in the report, if you follow me. That's the difficulty I have with the question, I suppose, is Mr. Hannis's objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there are two or three things here. First, the witness claims that he knew about it, but he did not wish to comment on it because this is something that other experts from the Prosecution were commenting on since they were co-operating within the Prosecutor's office and it was known which expert was covering which part of the testimony during a trial. This is the first thing. Second, we really must ask the witness this and on the basis of his positions we are telling him why we believe the division of the MUP occurred. His position is that this was the desire or the will of the Serbian cadres from the Serbian Democratic Party, and we are asserting the opposite. So we have to put this to the witness, with all due respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Except that the witness is not compelled to take on board in terms of the opinions which he has formed, and which is what his report is all about, the views of anybody else, including the views now being articulated by counsel. But I haven't lost sight of your continuing to put your case, to lay the foundation for the eventual Defence case. It's only in the interests of time, Mr. Zecevic, that the -- inviting the witness presently on the stand, to engage him in these detailed exchanges about, in this case, the Cutileiro report is -- is it helpful?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we believe that that part of the report of the witness is wrong, and we are putting questions to him with that premise, and we are putting to him why we believe that his report here is incorrect, but I see that Mr. Hannis is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The essence of my objection, I guess, Your Honours, is a procedural one, in effect. There's been a lot of talk in this case about the Cutileiro Plan or the Cutileiro agreement. Those terms have been used in loose fashion, and frankly, I have to confess it's not clear to me, I've heard several -- I've heard witnesses say there was no agreement. There was a conference. There were principles for negotiations, but if there is an agreement, if there is a document called the Cutileiro Plan or the Cutileiro agreement and he wants to ask him a question about that, then he should show him that document. So in fairness to the witness he sees what he's being asked about. But if he's just using his generic Cutileiro Plan or Cutileiro agreement term, the witness may not understand what that is. That's the essence of my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, the position - while we're on the same topic, to help the Trial Chamber, to help to some extent the witness - the position of Zupljanin Defence with regard to the Cutileiro Plan is as follows: Our case is based on the competence of the entities of Bosnia and Herzegovina regarding certain -- certain aspect of -- of government, including police. Three parties in Bosnia-Herzegovina, before the, let's say, adoption of draft of Cutileiro Plan, agreed that entities will form, have control, and conduct their own police forces. This is the beginning. This is the gist of this problem. And I'm almost hundred per cent, maybe hundred ten per cent sure that distinguish Dr. Nielsen is aware about that, that fact. So it's very narrow, Your Honours, use of principles and general framework for the future constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina. At the end of the day, as I mentioned on many occasions, these principles were enshrined in Dayton peace accord, whereas today we also have a sort of divided police controlled by the entities in Bosnia. And this is the sole and very limited issue with regard to the Cutileiro Plan. This is position of Zupljanin Defence, and I will announce this line, these several questions, now, I will announce for Dr. Nielsen during my cross. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nielsen --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Have you ruled then that he's not going to be required to show the document to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thought the last thing he said is that he's going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think he's planning to move on and ask him about the Cutileiro Plan without showing him a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said that I'm going to show the document to the witness. That is exactly what I intend to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D00-2708.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is your tab 27. Mr. Nielsen, the day before yesterday Mr. Hannis asked you about the Cutileiro Plan. I thought that in that sense he and I agree that that is the popular name for the document of the European Union that is called "Principles of New Constitutional Arrangements for Bosnia-Herzegovina." It is popularly known as the Cutileiro Plan because this plan -- or, rather, this attempt of making arrangements in Bosnia and Herzegovina on behalf of the European Union was spearheaded by Lord Carrington and the Foreign Minister of Portugal, Mr. Cutileiro. However, since Lord Carrington had worked out some other plans before that, in order to make a distinction between and among these plans this document is known as the Cutileiro Plan. I think that when Mr. Hannis put questions to you the day before yesterday, he was actually asking you about the Cutileiro Plan. Therefore, I do not understand the objection made by Mr. Hannis now. However --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My objection is Mr. Zecevic started out by talking about the Cutileiro Plan beginning in September 1991. This document is dated February 22nd, 1992. It does not say Cutileiro Plan on it. Mr. Zecevic has been trying to testify for you by saying this is popularly known as the Cutileiro Plan, et cetera. He's not a witness. He needs to ask a question. And if this is the Cutileiro Plan that he's referring to, I'm satisfied and Mr. Nielsen can talk about it, but I want to be sure that it wasn't some other document from September 1991 that was entitled "Cutileiro Plan."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, let me ask you something. Do you know that this plan of the European Union about the new constitutional arrangements for Bosnia-Herzegovina started in September 1991 under Lord Carrington and Mr. Cutileiro? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not exactly familiar with when it started.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. This document that you see now is a document that is called "Statement on Principles for New Constitutional Arrangements for Bosnia and Herzegovina." It is dated the 22nd of February, 1992. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and I comment on it in direct examination, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think it was this document. I'll show you the document that you commented on somewhat later. This document is dated the 22nd of February. I think that your comments had to do with the document dated the 18th of March, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The document dated the 22nd of February, just like the document that you commented upon dated the 18th of March, envisaged as basic postulates the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina that will consist of three entities, three constituent units; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is precisely what point 1 under heading (A) states, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then in this document under (D), and I think the situation is the same in the document that you commented upon dated the 18th of March, the rights and responsibilities of each entity are listed; inter alia, it says that laws will be passed and that different questions will be regulated, police included; right? Do you see that? (D)2. The one-but-last line?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this statement of principles does indeed contemplate that the entities, three of them, would run the police within an independent but unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I mean is that there continues to be a central state and a central assembly and government as is set out in the points under point (C). That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify this. This draft statement of principles for a new Bosnia and Herzegovina, et cetera, it envisages an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina consisting of three entities in the form of some federal state with the central government in Sarajevo and central ministries in Sarajevo. Isn't that right -- or, rather, isn't that your understanding of this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is a quite correct understanding and is reflected in the document before us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to have this document admitted into evidence, please, if there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 1D00-2708 shall be admitted as Exhibit 1D00133. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you document 1D01-0936 shall, please. Tab 28. I'm being told that it is the right time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I was about to bring to your attention [overlapping speakers] at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the witness is being escorted back in, we regret any inconvenience caused to counsel and the accused by our delay in taking the bench, but we were engaged in an urgent administrative matter relative to this trial. And while I'm interrupting the proceedings by way of explanation, when we resume tomorrow morning, we will be sitting under the provisions of Rule 15 bis for the first session and possibly the second. There is a commitment which I made before -- when the time was set for the afternoon, but I fully expect to be here for the third session. It remains to be seen whether I'm here for the second session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nielsen, just one question in relation to the previous document that we introduced as 1D133. That is the statement on principles for new constitutional arrangements for Bosnia-Herzegovina. It may be assumed, right, that this document was created on the basis of some previously agreed views among the parties concerned; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it is accurate to state, although I'm not an expert on international negotiations on the status of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that this document came to exist in the context of ongoing negotiations among the parties concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, Mr. Hannis showed you 65 ter number 26 -- 2767.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have that document called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 30 in your set. It is more or less identical to the number that we looked at just now; however, this one is dated the 18th of March. As opposed to the previous document, on the last page, and that is page 3 in e-court, confirms that agreement was reached among the leaders of the following parties: SDA, SDS, and HDZ, in the fifth round of negotiations on future agreements for Bosnia-Herzegovina under the auspices of the peace conference of the European Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Is there a problem with the document? We need the last page in the English version, please. The third page. I said that. Page 3. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, do you see this? The day before yesterday, you commented upon this with Mr. Hannis, and on page 4721, you established that in your view this was not an agreement but a set of principles as a basis for further talks. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it clearly says in capital letters: "This paper is the basis of further negotiations."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, Mr. Nielsen, on page 4732, you confirm that this document is an agreed framework for the future arrangements in Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I recall stating that -- that notwithstanding the representatives of the SDA, in particular Mr. Izetbegovic, later revoked his signature and agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I understood you correctly, you will agree with me that the signature on this document proves that the parties are prepared to observe the provisions of that document.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the document in front of us does not have anyone's signature on it, but, that -- yes, that is what would be the case if it were signed or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, is the 18th March version just a draft of the previous one we had? No, sorry, the previous one was 22nd February. That was a draft and this is the final version, is that it? Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly, Judge Harhoff. This document of the 18th of March was signed by the representatives of all three parties in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, when it is stated in a document that these are agreed facts and that the document is a basis for further negotiations, you will agree with me that these further negotiations pertain to some new additional questions that need to be clarified through further negotiations, not these that have already been signed. That is why this is called a statement on principles; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation of the words "basis of further negotiations" is that theoretically it is possible that such further negotiations could include both making more precise the points in this statement of principles, but also suggesting that some of them might be changed, and I would again point to the fact that Mr. Izetbegovic revoked his signature from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you have a very special characteristic. Namely, you draw conclusions on certain legal matters, and you give explanations with regard to matters that do not belong to your field of expertise, and in other situations when questions are put to you by counsel, you say that you're not a lawyer and that you cannot give your own comments; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's argumentative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I do apologise. I will withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Nielsen, do you have an education in the field of law?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have taken courses at Columbia University in international law, but I do not hold a law degree, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was that public international law or private, or was it criminal law? What field was it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took courses in what you would call public international law and specifically in the field of international criminal law and international humanitarian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on that basis you think that you have sufficient expertise to be able to comment upon such agreements? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection. That's argumentative as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you think, Mr. Nielsen, that on the basis of that course of yours at the University of Columbia you have sufficient knowledge to comment upon such agreements like the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thought, Mr. Zecevic, that you had taken Mr. Hannis's hint.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously I hadn't. I thought that this question was perfectly proper, Your Honour. I was asking the witness on which basis or, rather, whether he believes that on the basis of that course in international public law and international humanitarian law he is in a position to comment on these agreements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, is that a question that the witness can seriously be expected to answer? He has been tendered as an expert witness by the Prosecution. The Chamber has accepted him as an expert witness. Now, in terms of his professional training and experience, you can test him on that, but a question that begins with "Do you think," strikes me as one that is bound to fail.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, do you know what the Brussels agreement pertains to in the context of this statement on principles of the future arrangements for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware that a further round of talks, I believe it was called the sixth round of talks, took place in Brussels at the end of March 1992, as far as I recall, and I can only speculate that it -- that the "Brussels agreement" might refer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the term "the Sarajevo agreement" in that context?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with that term, and I believe that, if I'm not mistaken that, might well have been a local, that is to say Bosnian, term that referred to the same sixth round of negotiations, but that's again based on my general knowledge of the situation at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document. The day before yesterday it was used by Mr. Hannis, 65 ter 2767. I don't know. I don't know. I mean, I think that Mr. Hannis did not tender it. I don't know whether he intended to tender it along with this expert report, so I'm just seeking clarification before I tender it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, it's not a document listed in his expert report, and I didn't tender it yesterday. I have no objection to it being admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 02767 shall be admitted as Exhibit 1D134. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, in response to Mr. Hannis's question, you spoke about 65 ter document 38. Those are minutes from the meeting held in Banja Luka on the 11th of February, 1992. In your binder it is document 38. Sorry, 45. The page is 4725. If I may say so, you said in rather picturesque terms that this meeting is actually a birth certificate for the Serbian MUP. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you are incorrect in saying that, because the document that I referred to as the birth certificate for the Serbian MUP was the dispatch sent by Momcilo Mandic on 31st of March, 1992, and not the 11 February meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Mr. Nielsen, this document dated the 11th of February, 1992, from Banja Luka is a document where certain Serbian staff members of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina held a meeting; right? Just Serb personnel.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that you have looked at this document more than once. At least that's how I understood you. And you would agree with me that it mostly consists from remarks and the views of those present from the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP about the facts that we talked about earlier, you and I here during the session today in the courtroom; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These same problems that we dealt with in detail this morning were also troubling the persons attending this meeting. What I'm particularly interested in, and you did go through the document with Mr. Hannis and you commented on certain parts of it, what I'm interested in is page 2. I think it's the same page in the Serbian and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the e-court it's page 2, second paragraph from the top. I'm sorry. I apologise. It seems to me that it's actually on page 1 in the English version, this comment from Mico Stanisic's speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to appear - it's one paragraph but last - in -- what Mico Stanisic is noted to have said, and it begins: "A list of minimal outstanding demands should be assembled at this meeting and submitted to Minister Alija Delimustafic, with a reasonable deadline for their resolution." Mr. Nielsen do you considering that this meeting in Banja Luka on the 11th of February, between these members of the Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP was held in secret or not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In view of what Mr. Mico Stanisic says here that a list of outstanding demands should be assembled at this meeting and submitted to Minister Alija Delimustafic, that would indicate that there is no intention to keep this meeting secret; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. You and I could meet secretly and agree to provide information to a third party. So I don't think the fact that they agreed -- that they agreed to provide information to Delimustafic from the point of pure logic tells us whether it was a confidential or covert meeting or not. I have no view on whether it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the documents that you looked through while you were preparing your report, did you establish that the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP, or at least the leadership of the Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP, were familiar or informed about the formation of the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there are some indications in the documentation that I have reviewed that they were aware that Serbian personnel in SRBiH MUP were organising themselves. I note that many of those documents that refer to such activity refer to such activity as troubling and possibly illegal, but I do think that there was an awareness within SRBiH MUP that such activity was ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I think that at several points in your report you mention the media, which referred to the establishment of the MUP of Republika Srpska; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were reports in the media. I don't know which point in time you're precisely referring to, but there were certainly rumours in the media prior to April 1992 that indicated that the Serbs in SRBiH MUP were involved in possibly establishing their own Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact, Mr. Nielsen, that Republika Srpska was formed on the 9th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be logical to expect that a republic that is established would establish its own organs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends what kind of republic we're talking about and what the general political context is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I mean, please, if a republic is formed regardless of the context or regardless of the kind of republic that is involved, it still has to have its organs, does it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- if the people who are doing that are to achieve their ambitions, yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I mean if the representatives of a people decide to create a state and adopt such a decision at the Assembly, then it can be assumed, surely, that such a state would need to function, too, would it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, within the context of their own plans it indeed does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think that -- I think -- I think that there is no need to put the question to you anymore. This is so evident. Just one more question about this document. On page 8 of the Serbian version, and I think it's on page 7 of the English version, last item numbered 19. 65 -- I apologise. Item 19 which states: "Ensure maximum media coverage of our work and the decisions made about the Serbian MUP." Do you see that? This is one of the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me, then, that the people who attended this meeting wanted to inform the public information media about the formation of this republic for the purposes of having this state that was created on the 9th of January, 1992, to function.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his last sentence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, the -- the interpreters didn't catch your last sentence, so if you would be good enough to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document. It's document 65 ter 38. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 65 ter 38 shall be given Exhibit 1D135. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 64, line 22, I did not see the witness's answer in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I asked you if you would agree with me that the people who attended this meeting wanted to inform the public via the media about the forming of this ministry in the republic precisely because they wanted to show that the state that was created on the 9th of January, 1992, was functioning, and your answer that you gave was not recorded in the transcript. Could you please repeat it now?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Nielsen, now we're coming to that document. This is a dispatch signed by assistant minister of the interior Mr. Momcilo Mandic on the 31st of March, 1992, and it's number 022482. And it was sent to practically all the addresses of the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP; isn't that right? Do you recall this document? This is P353, and in your tab it is document -- just a moment, please. Forty-eight. P353, 65 ter 62. You commented on this document with Mr. Hannis the day before; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you to look at the upper left-hand corner where you can see the date. It's a telefax marking where the date is the 31st of March, 1992. And the time is 13.58 hours. There is the number -- the telephone number 071 276865. It says MUP, Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and then it was probably sent to radio Sarajevo. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I agree with your reading of the document on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please now show the witness document 65 ter 1301.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, that is -- this is a dispatch signed by the minister of the interior, Alija Delimustafic, in reaction to the previous document, P353, which was signed by his assistant, Mr. Momcilo Mandic. Do you see this document, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't appear to have that reaction dispatch. I'm familiar with it, but I don't appear to have it in the binder here in front of me. At least if it's if chronological order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not able to find it in the text, but in any case, you have it just like everybody else, on your monitor. I'm sure that you have looked at this document before.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dispatch on the monitor is still the one of Momcilo Mandic and not the one of Alija Delimustafic. Oh, now I see it. Yes, sir. I agree, yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document in which Alija Delimustafic speaks about the destructive effect of the dispatch on the unity of the MUP, the dispatch written by Momcilo Mandic, and then he says that he is not in a position to reflect on the regulations that it refers to because they are not known to the professional services or by the leading staff whose name is being mentioned in the dispatch, and then he asks that it should not be permitted that anybody splinters off from the rest of their MUP colleagues and so on and so forth. This is on page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This part that I drew your attention to begins with -- begins, actually, in the second paragraph of this document for the purposes of the English translation. Sir, on the first page of the document, and we see that in the B/C/S version, but if -- can we look at it in the English as well, you can see that the date when the document was sent is also the 31st of March. The document was sent at 13.59 hours. It also has the telefax number at the top, also the mark that it was sent by the Bosnia and Herzegovina Sarajevo MUP, and it can be seen that again it was sent to Radio Sarajevo. This means that between Momcilo Mandic's dispatch, which is P353 - and he is the assistant minister of the interior - and the reaction of the minister of the interior, Mr. Alija Delimustafic, there is only a one-minute difference in the -- between the time that the first and the second one was sent. Can we agree on that on the basis of looking at these two documents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that there was a one-minute difference between the time when the first and second was sent to Radio Sarajevo, but I do not necessarily agree that there was a one-minute difference between the time when Mandic wrote his dispatch and Delimustafic wrote his dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you. This is a fair conclusion. Keeping in mind what we said a little bit earlier about the conclusions of the 11th of February and the obvious need, I would say, for this dispatch by Momcilo Mandic to be published as early as possible, you could assume that Momcilo Mandic's intention was, first of all, to inform the public and the media about his dispatch, wouldn't you say?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suggest in my report that there are some very good reasons why Mr. Mandic was in a hurry to issue this dispatch on that given day. I deal with that at length. I agree that, certainly, he is trying to inform the public about it, and certainly Delimustafic is trying to do the same about his contrary opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this 65 ter document 1301 tendered if there are no objections from Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 01301, shall be admitted as 1D136. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, this is document 65 ter 1301.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, from the document that we have just looked at, one could conclude that Mr. Alija Delimustafic was opposed and disagreed with the division of the MUP from the dispatch of Mr. Momcilo Mandic.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: One would expect from the minister to represent the position of the ministry, wouldn't one?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and of the government of which he was a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: While you were preparing for the report and reviewing the documents, did you perhaps have a chance to look at any document on the basis of which you could conclude that the division of the MUP and the dispatch by Momcilo Mandic of March 31st, 1991, was completely in keeping with the position of the ministry of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not a chance -- had a chance to look at any such document on the basis of which I could reach that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness 1D78 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. I do not have this document in e-court. Can I have the 65 ter number, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am being warned that there is a mistake of some sort in the e-court, and so now we are going to call the document by its 65 ter number, 2768. And even though it does say in the transcript that it was admitted as one document, 1D178, we will not waste time on that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have this document in e-court as P00411.32.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, if I understand correctly, the document is in e-court and we will clarify this later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, the document's letterhead says "The Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." The date is the 1st of April, 1992. It's addressed to the ministers of the interior, Mico Stanisic and Alija Delimustafic, the MUP administrations at the headquarters, and then it is also sent to all the other addresses at the -- of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina. A copy was also sent to the federal SUP in Belgrade. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I would point out that I cite a version of this document in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the document that was sent to all the public security stations by one of the CSBs. Is that what you're thinking of?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If memory serves, this dispatch was forwarded to other subordinate units within MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will show you that. This is a document which states in a: "The reorganisation of the organs for internal affairs and their respective security services already taken place further to the Sarajevo agreement on possible future organisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was endorsed in general terms at the Brussels talks yesterday. In that respect, as you have already been advised, and in accordance with the constitution of the republic," and so on. And then it says -- we're talking about paragraph 2 now on the same page: "The following members of the current advisory board of the MUP discuss this matter on the 1st of April, 1992: Vitomir Zepinic, deputy minister; Branko Kvesic, under-secretary for the state security service." We saw that he was an HDZ candidate. "Jusuf Pusina, assistant minister for police." I hope that you would agree with me that he's a cadre of the SDA. Bruno Stojic. We saw that he was assistant minister for financial matters but was in the HDZ. Momcilo Mandic, assistant minister for crime prevention; Akif Sabic, assistant minister also; and Avdo Hebib, who is ministerial advisor for internal affairs; and Mico Stanisic, who is the minister the interior of the republic of the Serbian nation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As you can see, the dispatch by Momcilo Mandic, followed by the dispatch by Alija Delimustafic, were sent one after the other at an interval of a minute to all of these addresses. On the 1st of April, the MUP collegium had a meeting in which it discussed this matter. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I agree with you that they had a meeting in which they discussed this matter? Is that the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that on the basis of this document it appears that they had a meeting concerning the issues that are discussed in this dispatch. I think it's important to note that Mr. Delimustafic is notable by his absence at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree that Minister Delimustafic did not attend the meeting, but all his assistant ministers were there; right? Or at least a vast majority of them.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly a lot of them were present, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 it says, on page 2 of the English text, and it's all one page in the Serbian text, it says that Mico Stanisic familiarised the collegium with some aspects of the functioning of the security [indiscernible] specifying the reasons why the existing MUP did not function properly and so on and so forth. Then he says the professional collegium, realistically reviewing the situation and wanting to avoid conditions for possible further deterioration of the otherwise complex situation, took the view that without any excesses the MUP should be transformed peacefully and without any excesses - both in headquarters and the field - the facilities and equipment in the SJB and SDB in the territory of the republic must not be ceased by any single nation unilaterally, that the employees must not unilaterally be dismissed only because their national and political affiliations, and that employees are not to be coerced, et cetera. Also, due attention has been paid to the functioning of the financing of the newly established Ministry of the Interior of the republic of the Serb Nation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which shall not be below the existing level. Some personnel matters have been considered as well. Mr. Nielsen, this document shows that the professional collegium of the minister knew and realised that the MUP of the Bosnia and Herzegovina was being subdivided into two, and in the last subparagraph that I referred to they were even looking at the possibilities for financing the MUP of the Republika Srpska. And it also says here that it will not be below the existing level. That's the position of the collegium; right? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that that is to a large extent what this document says. I think it's again worth noting that this steering council or collegium of the ministry is meeting in the absence of the minister himself, and I think it's also significant to note that per the ongoing negotiations that we were discussing earlier today, the very first sentence refers to the possible future state organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that it's apparently contingent upon further negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, we discussed these negotiations, so we're not going to go back to that. I asked you specifically whether you agree with me that this is what is being stated in this document. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I do agree, but that is why I intend to put a question to the witness once he gives me an answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, can't you just proceed to put your question as -- I mean, we can all read what the document says. Put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you have this document in your possession when you were writing this report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and as I note, I cite a version of it in my report, the one that was forwarded, which is a verbatim forwarding of this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. You are trying to tell me that you had the original in mind but you did not cite it in your report, if I understand you correctly? You refer to a copy of that decision that one of the CSBs forwarded further in the field. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I am trying to say is that I cited another original document which quotes, in full, this particular document because reflecting, as you yourself put it, the final sentence of this document, the point was to acquaint all members of MUP, both in the field and in the ministry itself, with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What document do you mean, Mr. Nielsen? Could you give me a reference? The one that you're citing in your report, that is.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that it's going to be very difficult for me to find it immediately, but I can certainly -- I'm happy to inform you first thing in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. That's what I wanted to suggest since we have two or three minutes left before we conclude. Let me ask you one more thing. So we'll continue discussing this document. This document was exhibited as a Defence document, but the 65 ter -- but the OTP brought it up at the 65 ter meeting as well. You said you got documentation concerning the Cutileiro Plan from the OTP. What about this document? It was not -- it was not made available to you? You did not discuss it during your preparations? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became aware of this document because it's cited in my esteemed colleague Bajagic's report, and I noted that I was citing a different version of the same document or a very, very similar document with the same content in my own report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand what you mean. What report of Mr. Bajagic you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to his expert report in the Borovcanin case with which I'm familiar. He cites it in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, this document, in essence, does it not confirm my thesis, the one that I've been putting to you here; namely, that the division of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina is the result of a trilateral agreement reached among the representatives of the SDA, the SDS, and the HDZ -- or, rather, the Muslim, Croat, and Serb peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If one only reads this document in isolation, then I can see how you would reach that conclusion. However, taking all the documents which I have been able to review in toto, I do not concur with your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that this would be a good moment to break off, and then we can continue with Mr. Nielsen tomorrow. Thank you, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic, and -- and Dr. Nielsen, of course I remind you that you're still on your oath, and the usual -- sorry, the usually cautions apply, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So you're now released -- you're now excused, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, Registrar informs us that you've used three hours and five minutes of your time, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We are trying to do our best in order to finish as early as possible. However, we haven't been doing brilliantly regrettably. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Just for the Registrar, the Registrar now informs us that there was a mistake in the information that I just gave you. In fact, you have used five hours and ten minutes, I understand. So you've got about four hours left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, as I said, we are trying our best, but we might be required to ask for some, with the -- with the -- to some more time to deal with this witness. As you can see, it's fairly -- fairly important to -- with the matters that we deal with him. We would appreciate that from the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks. I just wanted to give you a head's up as to how far along --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I appreciate that very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand, and I'll try to limit my objections and keep them short in hopes that we can finish at least the cross-examination by the Stanisic Defence team before the winter recess. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Tomorrow, 9.00, in this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of December, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
